CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where should you walk beside the pool? (1 mark)
   A. On the pool side, walking slowly
   B. Jumping
   C. Running
   D. Sliding

2. A streamlined shape is (1 mark)
   A. round like a ball
   B. long and thin like an arrow
   C. bent like a chair
   D. wide and floppy

3. Outside the pool, in a river or the sea, you should (1 mark)
   A. go in at night
   B. swim alone
   C. dive from rocks
   D. only go in with a trusted adult who can swim

4. Water games help learners to (1 mark)
   A. study more
   B. feel comfortable in the water
   C. avoid the pool
   D. forget to swim

5. In the sit-and-slide entry, you should turn (1 mark)
   A. away from the wall
   B. to the deep end
   C. upside down
   D. to face the wall and hold the edge

6. Swimming is important because (1 mark)
   A. it replaces school
   B. it is a life skill that helps keep you safe near water
   C. it needs no rules
   D. it makes water disappear

7. Which Kiswahili word means elephant? (1 mark)
   A. twiga
   B. nyoka
   C. tembo
   D. kuku

8. Before animal games you should (1 mark)
   A. fight
   B. eat a big meal
   C. sleep
   D. warm up

9. Why do animal games often use singing or drumming? (1 mark)
   A. To hide the players
   B. To scare animals
   C. To stop the game
   D. Rhythm helps players move together and adds fun

10. Which game builds strong arms and shoulders as you crawl on hands and toes? (1 mark)
   A. Snake slither
   B. Elephant walk
   C. Crocodile crawl
   D. Giraffe stretch

11. Which Kiswahili word means snake? (1 mark)
   A. nyoka
   B. kuku
   C. chura
   D. tumbili

12. In a folk song, the soloist (1 mark)
   A. is silent
   B. is the audience
   C. plays the drum only
   D. leads and sings the call

13. A working portfolio holds (1 mark)
   A. balls
   B. food
   C. only finished prize work
   D. work in progress such as sketches and trials

14. Which value is found in the Kenya National Anthem? (1 mark)
   A. Laziness
   B. Selfishness
   C. Unity
   D. Cheating

15. To analyse a work of art means to (1 mark)
   A. ignore it
   B. paint over it
   C. throw it away
   D. look closely at its parts to understand it

16. The message of an art work is (1 mark)
   A. the artist's age
   B. the size of the frame
   C. what the artist wants us to learn or feel
   D. the price

17. What is used to close a homemade portfolio? (1 mark)
   A. Nails
   B. A string or ribbon tie
   C. A padlock
   D. Wet glue only

18. Aesthetic refers to (1 mark)
   A. how heavy it is
   B. how long it is
   C. how cheap it is
   D. how beautiful or pleasing something is

19. On which occasion may the national anthem be sung? (1 mark)
   A. A private joke
   B. Never
   C. Only at night
   D. Madaraka Day celebrations

20. How can you decorate a portfolio cover? (1 mark)
   A. By putting sand on it
   B. By pasting coloured paper or fabric
   C. By burning it
   D. By tearing it

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain why it is dangerous for a child to jump into a river to rescue someone. (3 marks)

22. Give four ways of caring for displayed works. (4 marks)

23. What does it mean to appreciate a work of Creative Arts? (2 marks)

24. State the role of the Kenya National Anthem. (3 marks)

25. Describe how to do the elephant walk. (3 marks)

26. How can an elder help you to learn indigenous games? (2 marks)

27. Describe how to make a portfolio from manila paper. (5 marks)

28. Why is it good to take different roles in animal games? (3 marks)

29. Describe how you would enter the pool and perform a glide safely. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #6 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — On the pool side, walking slowly
   Wet floors are slippery.

2. B — long and thin like an arrow
   A long shape slips easily through water.

3. D — only go in with a trusted adult who can swim
   Open water is more dangerous.

4. B — feel comfortable in the water
   They build confidence.

5. D — to face the wall and hold the edge
   You hold the edge as you lower yourself in.

6. B — it is a life skill that helps keep you safe near water
   Swimming helps prevent drowning.

7. C — tembo
   Tembo is an elephant.

8. D — warm up
   Warming up prepares muscles.

9. D — Rhythm helps players move together and adds fun
   Music sets the pace.

10. C — Crocodile crawl
   Body held straight on hands and toes.

11. A — nyoka
   Nyoka is a snake.

12. D — leads and sings the call
   The soloist starts or leads.

13. D — work in progress such as sketches and trials
   It shows how work develops.

14. C — Unity
   The anthem speaks of unity, peace, justice and service.

15. D — look closely at its parts to understand it
   Analysing means studying the parts.

16. C — what the artist wants us to learn or feel
   The message is the idea communicated.

17. B — A string or ribbon tie
   Punched holes with string keep it closed.

18. D — how beautiful or pleasing something is
   Aesthetic is about beauty.

19. D — Madaraka Day celebrations
   It is sung on national days and at official events.

20. B — By pasting coloured paper or fabric
   Decorating uses local resources.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: The child may also drown because water can be deep or fast. It is safer to shout for an adult and throw something that floats.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the danger, 2 marks for the safe action.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Do not touch or write on them; keep away from water, sun and dust; keep neat labels; store in the portfolio flat afterwards. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: To notice, understand and value it, giving reasons for what you think.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is a national symbol that unites Kenyans, shows love for the country and reminds us of our values.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bend forward at the waist, clasp hands so that the arms hang like a trunk, and walk slowly with heavy steps, swaying the trunk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: The elder can teach you the games and songs of the community and share their stories.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Fold two large pieces of manila paper to make a folder and trim the edges. Punch holes and add a string tie. Paste coloured paper or fabric on the cover. Write a label with name and class. Put in the works with dates and notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of the five parts.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Everyone gets a fair turn, learns to lead and follow, and the team works better.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

29. (5 marks)
   Answer: Get permission and warm up. Enter feet first by the steps or sit and slide. Stay in shallow water. Stand with the back to the wall and stretch the arms overhead. Put feet on the wall, breathe, put the face in, push off gently and glide with a straight body.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of five parts.
